sourceNote: Selective DGT editorial notes. UBS5/NA28 comparisons are based on the SBLGNT apparatus; UBS5 and NA28 share the same base text in 1 John.

1:1: The opening repeatedly uses the neuter relative ὅ, “what,” before speaking of “the Word of life.” DGT preserves that concrete eyewitness phrasing rather than changing it immediately to “whom.”
2:1: παράκλητος is the same word family used of the Spirit in John 14–16. Here the courtroom sense is prominent, so DGT uses “advocate.”
2:2: ἱλασμός describes the sin-dealing efficacy of Christ’s sacrifice. English choices such as “atoning sacrifice,” “propitiation,” and “expiation” emphasize different aspects of the term.
3:6: The present-tense ἁμαρτάνει is naturally read as ongoing or characteristic action in this context. DGT therefore uses “does not keep sinning,” rather than suggesting that a believer never commits a sin; compare 1:8–2:1.
3:9: As in 3:6, the present forms ποιεῖ and ἁμαρτάνει concern the practice or pattern of sin. DGT makes that aspect explicit with “keep practicing sin/keep sinning.”
4:9: μονογενής describes the Son as unique or one-of-a-kind. DGT uses “unique Son”; the word itself does not require the English phrase “only begotten.”
5:6: “Water and blood” has generated several interpretations. DGT leaves John’s compact wording intact rather than choosing an interpretation in the translation itself.
5:7: The familiar later wording about the Father, Word, and Holy Spirit in heaven—the so-called Comma Johanneum—is not present in SBLGNT or UBS5/NA28. The critical text simply says, “there are three who testify,” continuing in verse 8 with the Spirit, water, and blood.
5:18: SBLGNT reads αὐτόν, “keeps him,” naturally making the one born from God the protector of the believer. UBS5/NA28 reads ἑαυτόν, “keeps himself.” DGT follows SBLGNT here.
5:20: The final οὗτός, “this one,” can grammatically point to the immediately preceding Jesus Christ, though interpreters also relate it to “the True One.” DGT keeps the demonstrative explicit rather than silently resolving the referent.
